Items.Authors: David Blanquez, Jan Petersen, Desiree D. M. Ferreira, Denis Tcherniak, Gabriel Cobos Tello, Alessandro Morello
Items.Title: Lisa PMS: power supply module design and development
Items.Abstract: We present a technical status on the development of the Power Supply Module (PSM) of the Phasemeter Measurement System (PMS) for LISA. We provide a description of the overall module architecture, input and output connections, updated individual component design, specific progress on housekeeping and OVP/OCP circuitry, and an early design of the custom DC/DC converters necessary for the mission’s high demanding requirements.

Items.Authors: Robert J. Harris, Philipp Hottinger, Jonathan Crass, Philipp I. Dietrich, Christian Koos
Items.Title: Long-term performance of the MLR-TT sensor:two-photon polymerization validation in the telescope environment
Items.Abstract: We report on the long-term optical performance of the MLR-TT sensor backed by repeated measurements over the last four years since the sensor was first tested on-sky at the Large Binocular Telescope.  The goal of this demonstration is to assess the feasibility of the underlying technology of two-photon polymerization for future instrumentation in the harsh environment of astronomical telescopes.

Items.Authors: Suijian Xue, Lingtong Zhang, Boqian Xu
Items.Title: LOTUS: L2 orbital telescope for ultraviolet spectroscopy
Items.Abstract: This talk introduces the ongoing conceptual development of a 2-meter class space ultraviolet (UV) mission, featuring high sensitivity, spectroscopy, and pointing capabilities covering the far-ultraviolet (FUV, 90–350 nm) band. It aims to address core astrophysical questions regarding the ionized interstellar/intergalactic medium, hot stellar atmosphere physics, and UV radiation fields impacting planetary environments.    The China Space Station Telescope (CSST), launching in 2027, will leave valuable engineering legacies—silicon carbide mirror blanks, AIT (Assembly, Integration, and Test) facilities, and mission operation experience—for future space astronomy projects. Leveraging these resources, China’s advanced UV mirror coating technologies and recent progress in back-illuminated CMOS detectors enable a feasible, cost-effective dedicated space UV mission, empowering the astronomical community with new capabilities to explore the FUV universe.

Items.Authors: Iain A. Steele, Sofía Díez Ocharan, Miguel R. Alarcon, João Bento, Helen Jermak, Stuart Bates, Beth Garton, Miquel Serra-Ricart
Items.Title: LOTUS-X: transplanting the LOTUS spectrograph from the Liverpool Telescope to the Two-meter Twin Telescope
Items.Abstract: LOTUS was a UV optimized low resolution spectrograph mounted on the 2-m Liverpool Telescope (LT) between 2015 and 2019. It operated in fully robotic mode and with a fixed-format meaning no moving parts. Acquisition was accomplished using the main imager in conjunction with a deployable and rotating folding mirror within the LT A&G box. Here we describe a project (LOTUS-X) to transfer LOTUS to the TTT 2-m robotic telescopes. We show how the installation of a small angle wedge prism following the camera lens allowed shifting of the optimal wavelength range from the near-UV to the mid-visible waveband while maintaining image quality. The task of acquiring the target onto the spectrograph slit was the most challenging aspect of the project, requiring the development of a simple A&G box for TTT that uses a dichroic mirror to provide an acquisition image to a separate camera and to allow autoguiding on the science target.

Items.Authors: Mark Ferrier, Christian Schwab, David Coutts, Matt Owers, Jacob Pember, Andrew Monson, Chad Bender, David Sand, Duncan Wright
Items.Title: Low-resolution, high-throughput spectrometers for rapid transient follow-up with robotic telescopes
Items.Abstract: Transient astronomy is becoming increasingly important as large-scale survey facilities, such as the Vera Rubin Observatory, identify large numbers of time-sensitive events. The demand for spectroscopic follow-up now far exceeds available capacity, particularly for rapid response. We report on the development of a very high-efficiency, low-resolution spectrograph designed for small to medium (<1.5 m) sized telescopes. Its high throughput allows smaller telescopes to compete with larger facilities, while providing access to increased and more flexible telescope scheduling. It achieves this with affordable system cost, a compact spectrograph design, and broad deployability across existing facilities. Examples for suitable facilities are the robotic 0.8 m MARVEL telescopes at the MERCATOR Observatory in La Palma, Spain, and the robotic 0.8m RAPTOR telescope at Mt. Kent Observatory, Australia.

Items.Authors: David J. Sahnow, Christian I. Johnson
Items.Title: LP-Infinity: overcoming limits to the number of lifetime positions in the COS FUV channel
Items.Abstract: Since the Cosmic Origins Spectrograph (COS) was installed on the Hubble Space Telescope (HST) in 2009, thousands of spectra have been collected with the Far Ultraviolet (FUV) channel. Due to gain sag in the cross delay line detector, regular adjustments to the positions of the spectra have been made, with the seven and eighth becoming available in October 2025. Since the onboard flight software limited the number of Lifetime Positions to eight, it was necessary to develop a new method for implementing additional LPs to avoid reassigning previously used positions. This novel strategy, dubbed LP-Infinity, allows an effectively unlimited number of LPs that is now constrained only by the available detector real estate, allowing COS to continue obtaining high-quality FUV spectra well into the 2030s. We discuss the conception, development and implementation of LP-Infinity, its initial use in Cycle 33, and the plans for future LPs starting in 2027.

Items.Authors: Natalia Arteaga-Marrero, Auxiliadora Padrón-Brito, Salvador Pérez del Pino, Max Johann Dobat, Adrián Sánchez-Chaves, Diego Tamayo-Guzmán, Jordi Iborra Luis, Patricia Fernández-Izquierdo, Nicolas Lodieu, Jeff Kuhn
Items.Title: Machine learning-driven autonomous control of the distributed aperture for the small exo-life finder (SELF) telescope
Items.Abstract: The Small Exo-Life Finder (SELF) is a 3.5 m hybrid-interferometric telescope conceived as a prototype for the future Exo-Life Finder (ELF), a next-generation telescope designed to detect bio- and technosignatures through direct imaging. SELF employs a distributed-aperture architecture comprising 15 independently controlled primary mirrors, each paired with a secondary mirror. The complex optical and mechanical degrees of freedom require machine-learning-driven control for precise alignment. A convolutional neural network was implemented to learn the nonlinear relationship between sub-aperture tip-tilt and piston perturbations and their corresponding focal-plane signatures. The approach was evaluated using both simulations and measurements acquired with a laboratory demonstrator, referred to as nanoELF. The results demonstrated accurate tip-tilt estimation and identified the conditions required for piston recovery.

Items.Authors: Natalia Auricchio, Joseph Huesler, Simonetta Chinellato, Daniele Brienza, Gonzalo Ramos Zapata, Fernando Conde García, Amaia Santiago Pé, Lionel Lourit, Nathalie Gorter, Ricardo Bolt, Aline Hermans, Ilina Kondofersky, Giacomo Cherchi, Nicolas Gorius, Gianalfredo Nicolini, Flavia Calderone, Isabella Pagano, Elisabetta Tommasi
Items.Title: Management of the product assurance activities for PLATO camera
Items.Abstract: PLATO (PLAnetary Transits and Oscillations of stars) is an M3 medium-class space mission in ESA Cosmic Vision program devoted to detecting and studying a large number of extrasolar planetary systems. The launch window is planned for early 2027 from Europe’s Spaceport in French Guiana. The Payload includes 26 wide field-of-view Cameras, each observing a specific part of the sky, with the associated data processing units and power supply units. All 26 cameras were delivered to the Prime and integrated into the Optical Bench. The PLM was successfully connected to the SVM, which houses the systems operating the spacecraft.   This work outlines the status of Product Assurance activities at the end of serial production, when the cameras were shipped to the Prime, and in preparation for the AR. Specifically, we will describe the dedicated PA/QA structure that has been established to meet the project specific requirements, including the inspections, NCRs/RFXs management and cleanliness control.

Items.Authors: GyeongGon Bahk, Yunjong Kim, Jihun Kim, Heuisung Cho, Seunghyuk Chang, Dohoon Kim, Kyohoon Ahn, Il Kweon Moon, Yeonsik Kim, Hyuksun Kwon, Daewook Kim, Woowon Byun, Kwang-Il Seon, Yongseok Lee, Sang-Mok Cha, Jongyeob Park, Hong Soo Park, Gayoung Lee, Seonwoo Kim, Seri Yeon, Jongwan Ko
Items.Title: Manufacturable tolerance budget for the K-DRIFT G2
Items.Abstract: KASI Deep Rolling Imaging Fast Telescope Generation 2 (K-DRIFT G2) is a linear-astigmatism-free three-mirror system (LAF-TMS) utilizing off-axis freeform optics, designed for a sounding rocket mission to observe low surface brightness (LSB) objects. A dichroic beam splitter (DBS) has been added to the system for simultaneous observation of UV and visible light; the UV light reflects at the DBS, while the visible light transmits at the DBS. The rear surface of the DBS is configured to correct residual aberrations of the transmitted visible light through its freeform shape. In essence, K-DRIFT G2 has become an optical system where all components are composed of freeform surfaces, leading to expected high technical difficulty in the actual fabrication process. Therefore, this study aims to discuss the procedure for establishing the tolerance budget for the efficient fabrication of this all-component off-axis freeform optical system.

Items.Authors: Warren B. Foster, Ronald Appels, Melanie Sisco, Chad F. Bender, Richard Wortley, Roger Angel, Gilberto Chavez Lopez, Kevin Gilliam, Peter Gray, Andy Monson, Jason Patrou
Items.Title: Mass production of the LFAST 0.76m primary mirrors: fabrication tradeoffs and on-sky control
Items.Abstract: The Large Fiber Array Spectroscopic Telescope provides large collecting aperture at low cost. Individual 0.76m, f/3.3 spherical mirrors focus light into fibers that combine at a central spectrograph. Mirrors are slumped, ground on Trizact pads and polished on pitch using interferometric metrology. A large 32:1 aspect ratio was chosen to reduce material cost but leads to characteristic print-through errors. We present a process that balances tradeoffs between different fabrication methods to achieve 80% encircled energy in a 1.4arcsec fiber within a one-week cycle time.  Twenty mirrors are integrated onto a common tracking mount and supported with passive whiffle trees. While on-sky, gravity vector and thermal variations cause figure errors that are measured with focal plane wavefront sensing and corrected with perimeter Peltier devices. This 20x prototype will have a 3.4m equivalent collecting area and establishes a roadmap towards a future order of magnitude increase in aperture size.

Items.Authors: Simone Doniselli, Matteo Aliverti
Items.Title: MAVIS: cooling deformable mirrors using a Ranque–Hilsch vortex tube: prototyping and performance assessment
Items.Abstract: This work presents the prototyping and performance characterization of a Ranque–Hilsch Vortex Tube (RHVT) cooling concept for the deformable mirrors of the MAVIS Adaptive Optics Module. Tests conducted under the flow-limited conditions of the VLT infrastructure show that RHVT performance depends strongly on cold-mass fraction, inlet flow, and downstream pressure. Temperature drops of ~–20 °C and cooling powers of ~8 W were achieved, meeting MAVIS requirements. The results confirm that RHVT cooling is feasible if carefully tuned and integrated with appropriate pipeline sizing, insulation, and on-site calibration.

Items.Authors: Simone Doniselli, Matteo Aliverti, Davide Greggio
Items.Title: MAVIS: mechanical characterization of binding materials for cemented optics under thermal stress
Items.Abstract: This work presents a systematic mechanical characterization of silicone- and epoxy-based polymeric binding materials used in cemented optics. Using BK7 samples tested under controlled shear loading and relaxation, we derived shear modulus and viscoelastic parameters as a function of adhesive-layer thickness. Silicone materials showed thickness-independent mechanical behavior, while epoxies exhibited strong thickness dependence. The very low viscoelastic index (~10⁻³) confirms that linear elasticity is adequate for most analyses. These results provide practical guidelines for selecting and modelling adhesives in thermally stressed astronomical optical assemblies.

Items.Authors: Derya Öztürk Çetni, Taner Tarıık Aytaş, Ersen Balcı, Ebru Uzunçam, Naime Sude Börekçi, İlayda Ekinci, Dilara Demirci, Bilal Arslan, Muhammed Baki Bayram, Elif Temel, Berkay Şahin, Gizay Yolalan, Ramazan Şahin, Cahit Yeşilyaprak
Items.Title: Measurement of controlled turbulence effects on the optical path and Zernike modal analysis in a laboratory environment
Items.Abstract: This study aims to evaluate the performance of optical systems under laboratory-controlled atmospheric turbulence. A collimated beam passes through a turbulence generator, and the resulting wavefront distortions are measured using a Shack-Hartmann WFS. Along the same path, a focal plane camera records the beam profiles, which are analyzed in terms of Cn² and Zernike modes. This approach allows for systematic turbulence control and comparison with theoretical models.   The results evaluate the effect of turbulence on performance by revealing correlations between the Zernike modes obtained from the WFS and the focal plane images. The work provides a laboratory framework for investigating the contribution of varying turbulence conditions to the low-order Zernike aberrations typically associated with active optics in medium and large aperture telescopes.

Items.Authors: Christian Schwab, Glen Douglass, David Coutts, Dane Zielinski-Nicolson, Julian Stuermer
Items.Title: Measuring the dispersion of an etalon for wavelength calibration using an optical spectrum analyser
Items.Abstract: The performance of etalon-based calibration sources for precision spectroscopy depends on understanding their intrinsic dispersion and how that dispersion evolves over time. This work presents a practical methodology for measuring etalon dispersion using a commercial Redstone OSA, with specific relevance to high-precision radial-velocity (RV) spectrograph calibration.  High-resolution transmission spectra of Fabry–Perot etalons are recorded across the visible and near-IR band, enabling precise extraction of the wavelength-dependent spacing of successive resonances and reconstruction of the cavity’s effective dispersion curve. This informs coating designs, as well as strategies to measure the long term drift behaviour of the etalon. As the OSA references the peak measurements back to a reference laser, it provides independent, accurate measurements of the wavelength of each individual mode.

Items.Authors: Hang Zhan, Song-Hao Li, Qi Feng, Hong-fei Zhang, Jian Wang
Items.Title: Mechanical design of CMOS camera for irradiation test in space application
Items.Abstract: In modern space exploration missions, CMOS detectors are widely used in scenarios such as astronomical observation and deep-space exploration. They need to work stably for a long time in extreme space environments characterized by low temperature, vacuum, and high radiation. When the detector is exposed in the space radiation environment, irradiation by high-energy particles is likely to cause degradation of its performance. Therefore, it is essential to verify performance of the detector through the irradiation test using a CMOS camera with special design. In this talk, we will present the mechanical design of CMOS camera using GS1517 for Irradiation Test, including the vacuum sealing, support structure for the detector inside vacuum Dewar, Titanium Window and Irradiation Shielding.

Items.Authors: Matthew Ramirez, Hanshin Lee, Uma Subash
Items.Title: Mechanical designs, thermo-mechanical tests, laboratory evaluation of the 50-channel pilot absolute multiline system for the Hobby-Eberly Telescope edge sensor upgrade
Items.Abstract: This 25-year old SAMS (Old SAMS) has been showing obsolescence and performance/maintenance deficiencies and hence is undergoing an upgrade. To take the full advantage of this new system and its capabilities, we set out to design the kinematic mounts for the AMS channel components, to evaluate different adhesives for bonding the mounts to the back surfaces of the Zerodur mirror segments, to characterize the overall performance of the pilot AMS, and to assess the dynamic alignment control algorithms and software tools. The adhesive test requires mechanical testing under different environmental conditions that includes thermal cycles and tensile/shear stress. The mirror will also be tilted at 55 degrees to simulate the average tilt angle of mirror segments at the HET. In this paper, we discuss the mechanical designs, thermo-mechanical tests of adhesives, and laboratory evaluation of the 50-channel pilot AMS.

Items.Authors: Dane Zielinski-Nicolson, Christian Schwab, James Downes, David Coutts, Julian Stürmer, Glen Douglass, David Inglis
Items.Title: Metal and alloy IAD mirror coatings for Fabry Perot interferometers used in spectrometer calibration systems
Items.Abstract: This project evaluates whether metal and alloy-based mirror coatings can avoid the chromatic drift observed in dielectric-coated Fabry-Perot interferometers. Using TMM simulations, we identified candidate coating compositions, and we used Ion Assisted Deposition (IAD) to create adhesion layers and alloy cores forming semi-transparent mirrors covering the visible to near-IR. We measured surface roughness with an optical profiler and determined optical constants by ellipsometry. We then built an air-gap etalon and tested it with broadband collimated sources, recording spectra with a high-resolution Fourier-transform OSA. Our IAD metal/alloy coatings produced etalons with broad spectral coverage, and sufficient finesse and throughput.

Items.Authors: Johannes Algera, Pierre Piron, Jérôme Loicq, Tiberiu Ceccotti, Bogdan Vasilescu
Items.Title: Metasurface for broadband division of aperture polarimetry
Items.Abstract: The new space sector has experienced significant growth due to reduced launch costs and the miniaturization of satellites. Spectro-polarimeters usually require multiple optical elements and moving parts. In this work, we propose a transmissive metasurface component for miniaturizing spectro-polarimeters meant for the visible spectrum. Our metasurface component is divided into discrete birefringent waveplates in the vertical direction and performs spectral dispersion in the horizontal direction. After the metasurface, a linear polarizer converts the polarization modulation into an intensity modulation. The work is further divided into first manufacturing a metasurface just for polarimetry and later a metasurface just for spectral dispersion. Both functionalites will be later merged into one element. We present here the simulation of a metasurface that performs the polarimetry function.

Items.Authors: Wengfei Liu, Jiahao Zhou, Hongzhuan Hu, Haoyang Zhang, Jianping Wang, Zhigang Liu, Jiaru Chu, Ping Zhang, Zengxiang Zhou
Items.Title: Method for distinguishing and labeling multiple foreground objects in image data streams

Items.Authors: Xingda Chen, Jing Luo, Jihong Dong, Xiaohui Zhang
Items.Title: Method to mitigate polarization aberration in astronomical telescopes
Items.Abstract: Due to the demand for high-resolution imaging, polarization aberrations become a critical error source in astronomical telescopes. However, mitigating them involves complex trade-offs with other metrics. In this paper, two independent mitigation methods are proposed to address this issue. One is a low-polarization design method based on a genetic algorithm, where three free design parameters of off‑axis three‑mirror systems are optimized to minimize wave and polarization aberrations simultaneously. The other is a plane‑mirror‑based polarization compensation method, in which polarization aberrations are compensated by introducing plane mirrors with precisely controlled orientations, without affecting wave aberrations. Low‑polarization design results show that polarization aberrations are reduced by a factor of three. Compensation results show that polarization aberrations are reduced to approximately half. These examples demonstrate the effective of the proposed methods.

Items.Authors: Sachin Joshi, Benoît Sassolas, Edoardo Cucchetti, Pierre-Antoine Frugier, Sihem Sayah, Nicolas Theret, Christophe Latry, Pierre-Alain Goulm, Matthieu Castelnau, Luis M. Gaspar Venancio, Laurent Pinard, Anne Ealet
Items.Title: Metrology of EUCLID’s dichroic plate using the OBSERVE test bench: Initial PSF characterization using phase diversity
Items.Abstract: Multilayer dichroic plates can introduce wavelength-dependent variations of the wavefront errors (WFE) and affect the point spread function (PSF) of the imaging system due to non-uniformities in its coating layers. To characterize the WFE and the PSF of the dichroic plate, a metrology test bench – OBSERVE - has been developed for the Euclid mission by Imagine Optic and is operated at Laboratoire des Matériaux Avancés (LMA), Lyon. It consists of a Shack-Hartmann (SH) sensor and a PSF imaging camera. The bench performance with measurement reproducibility within a 6-7 nm root mean square (RMS) range has already been reported. To crosscheck these results and obtain more information about the PSF, we are performing phase diversity calibration of the PSF channel. We report the preliminary results of PSF channel calibration and ongoing experimental validation, which will be used for future WFE characterization of Euclid’s dichroic spare and can be generalized to dichroic metrology studies.

Items.Authors: Gayoung Lee, Jongwan Ko, Daewook Kim, Yunjong Kim, Jihun Kim, Woowon Byun, Kyohoon Ahn, Dohoon Kim
Items.Title: Mid-to-high spatial frequency surface error analysis for three-mirror off-axis freeform system
Items.Abstract: We developed the KASI Deep Rolling Imaging Fast Telescope (K-DRIFT), an off-axis freeform three-mirror system optimized for low-surface-brightness (LSB) observations. During on-sky observations, complex anisotropic scattering patterns were identified in the wings of saturated stellar images. To investigate their origin, interferometrically measured mirror surfaces were decomposed into spatial-frequency bands using Fourier filtering, and frequency-dependent point spread function (PSF) simulations were performed. The simulations show that fabrication-induced mid-to-high spatial-frequency errors, including residual tool-path signatures, are the primary source of the observed directional scattering structures. These results establish a direct link between mirror fabrication errors and PSF-wing degradation, emphasizing the need to control high-order surface errors in freeform optical systems.

Items.Authors: Christian Robles, Suvrath Mahadevan, Lawrence Ramsey
Items.Title: MiraSOL: a DMD-based spectrograph for resolved solar spectroscopy
Items.Abstract: We present the design requirements, device laboratory testing and a prototype for an upcoming solar instrument, MiraSOL. MiraSOL will use digital micromirror technology to actively select regions on the solar disk for spectroscopic observation to determine the spatially dependent radial velocity signatures of stellar variability. MiraSOL uses the Texas Instruments DLP801RE as a spatial light modulator to allow a 3 arcsecond resolution mask capable of resolving features on the solar disk. This instrument will have a fiber output which can then be coupled with state-of-the-art extreme precision radial velocity (EPRV) spectrometers, such as HPF or NEID, for high resolving power, stable spectra of sunspots and plage. We discover a 60 Hz flicker signal in the commercial digital micromirror device electronics. We also build a proof-of-concept prototype and acquire solar observations to demonstrate the feasibility of this technology.

Items.Authors: John C. Mather, Eliad Peretz, Rhonda M. Morgan
Items.Title: Mission design for HOEE (Hybrid Observatory for Earthlike Exoplanets)
Items.Abstract: The 39 m ELT with visible band adaptive optics, working with a 100 m diameter orbiting starshade, could image an exo-Earth at 5 pc distance in 1 minute, and get a spectrum of water and oxygen in an hour. With resolution of 3 milliarcsec, and contrast of 10^-11, detection is unambiguous. The ELT/starshade hybrid enables measurements that are otherwise impossible, for speed, resolution, and contrast. With solar electric propulsion to manage the orbit, matching velocity with the ELT, and changing orbit for each new target, we observe a target each five day orbit. With chemical propulsion, we hold alignment for hours for spectroscopy. With a new mechanical design for a 1500 kg starshade, plus supporting hardware and fuel, this mission is now possible, and could make the first detection of Earth 2.0. We present the mission concept, including mechanical design and deployment, operations, tolerances, and performance estimates.

Items.Authors: Carmelo Arcidiacono, Francesca Annibali, Paolo Ciliegi, Elisa Portaluri, Marco Gullieuszik, Michele Cantiello
Items.Title: MORFEO @ ELT: large-field, high-sensitivity astronomy for the ELT era
Items.Abstract: MORFEO (Multi-conjugate adaptive Optics Relay For ELT Observations) is the post-focal adaptive optics module for the ESO Extremely Large Telescope. The instrument provides MCAO correction for two instruments: MICADO and HARMONI.   By exploiting multiple lasers and natural guide stars together with several deformable mirrors conjugated to different atmospheric layers, MORFEO will deliver diffraction-limited image quality over a large, well-corrected field of view, uniform PSF and high sensitivity for the vast majority of the sky.  In this contribution, we describe the science programme crafted to maximize the scientific return of MORFEO + ELT. We present key science cases spanning deep imaging of distant galaxies, resolved stellar populations in the Milky Way and nearby galaxies, precise astrometry for dynamical studies, and time-domain observations of variable or transient objects. We outline observing strategies, expected performance, and highlight how MORFEO opens new discovery space.

Items.Authors: Gabriele Umbriaco, Paolo Ciliegi, Andrea Comastri, Andrea Di Rocco, Ludovico Teodori, Giuseppe Cosentino, Italo Foppiani, Gabriele Rodeghiero, Cristiano Spisni, Federico De Sanctis, Cristiano Guidi, Luca Rosignoli, Alessio Taranto, Sophie Antonia Penger, Jacopo Farinato, Luca Marafatto, Edoardo Maria Alberto Redaelli, Chiara Salvadori
Items.Title: MORFEO @ ELT: The Bologna Integration Hall for MORFEO, a national AIT infrastructure for ELT-class instrumentation
Items.Abstract: MORFEO (Multi-conjugate adaptive Optics Relay For ELT Observations) is the post-focal adaptive optics module for the ESO Extremely Large Telescope. The instrument provides MCAO correction for two instruments: MICADO and HARMONI.    The newly refurbished Bologna Integration Hall (BIH) supports MORFEO’s Assembly, Integration, and Verification, enabling the alignment and calibration of its complex optical train, which features ~1-m free-form, deformable, and spherical mirrors, using high-precision metrology such as laser trackers. The facility features a 12×17×12 m ISO 8 hall, optical and electronic labs, a mechanical workshop, and a control room, all equipped with upgraded cooling, power distribution, environmental monitoring, and lifting systems under PNRR STILES investments. Ongoing upgrades include enhancements to cranes, roof insulation, external platforms, and improved networking. BIH will host MORFEO before shipment to Chile

Items.Authors: Marco Xompero, Nicolò Azzaroli, Paolo Ciliegi, Lorenzo Busoni, Simonetta Chinellato, Giorgio Pariani, Roberto Biasi, Laura Salvi, Dietrich Pescoller, Matteo Tintori, Pierluigi Fumi, Lorenzo Crimella, Samson Sambath Kumar, Gabriele Clerici
Items.Title: MORFEO post-focal deformable mirrors: manufacturing and assembly phase following FDR success
Items.Abstract: MORFEO (Multi-conjugate adaptive Optics Relay For ELT Observations) is the post-focal adaptive optics module for the ESO Extremely Large Telescope. The instrument provides MCAO correction for two instruments: MICADO and HARMONI. The core of the MCAO correction are two Post Focal Deformable Moirros of 1m class monolithic mirrors with more than 1000 actuators for each one. The first is convex, 930 mm clear aperture while the second is concave 1224 mm clear aperture. Both DM successfully passed the Final Design Review in early 2025 and they are now in the assembly phase.

Items.Authors: Ivan Zavala, Joel Castro, Mauricio Reyes, Ana de la Llata, Javier Hernández, Gerardo Sierra, Félix Diaz, Francisco Valenzuela, Luis Ortiz, Joel Herrera, Francisco Murillo, David Hiriart
Items.Title: Multi-band high-cadence imaging at OAN-SPM: design and software architecture of the 2CAN VIS–SWIR instrument
Items.Abstract: The 2CAN instrument is a dual-channel VIS–SWIR imaging system for the 1.5-m telescope at the San Pedro Mártir Observatory (OAN-SPM). It enables simultaneous high-cadence observations in the visible (400–900 nm) and short-wave infrared (950–1650 nm) using an Andor iXon 888 or Zyla 5.5 in the VIS arm and a Raptor Ninox 640 SU in the SWIR arm. A dichroic beam splitter, dual filter wheels, a VIS focusing stage, and an optical-path compensator support multi-band science, including NEO taxonomic studies, stellar occultations, and asteroid phase-curve measurements. The custom software provides synchronized camera control, a graphical interface, GPS-based timing, hardware triggering, and real-time telemetry. Bench tests confirm successful parallel imaging and the timing performance required for rapid photometry. Once deployed, 2CAN will be the first instrument at OAN-SPM capable of fast SWIR photometry, enhancing time-domain and planetary-science capabilities.

Items.Authors: John J. Hennessy, Mitchell Kallas, Fernando Cruz Aguirre, Keri Hoadley, Sarah Tuttle
Items.Title: Multilayer dielectric coatings for ultraviolet instrumentation
Items.Abstract: We describe the development of new atomic layer deposition (ALD) processes for high refractive index materials like HfF4, LaF3, and ZrF4 with the goal of utilizing them for multilayer optical coatings operating at UV wavelengths. These multilayer structures can be used in the fabrication of narrowband mirror coatings operating in the challenging far UV portion of the spectrum. Continued development in this area is of interest to a number of NASA Astrophysics applications including the smallsat concepts Maratus and UVIa. A 20-layer AlF3/LaF3 mirror coating is demonstrated and achieves an average reflectance of greater than 90% for wavelengths between 135 and 140 nm. We present the results of initial aging studies that subject these films to elevated temperature and humidity.

Items.Authors: Hanshin Lee, Uma Subash, Samir Paudel, Menelaos K. Poutous, Michael P. Smith, Brian L. Vattiat
Items.Title: Multiple-aperture grating pattern inscription engine: UV pattern lithography tool for reactive ion-plasma etched large diffraction gratings and beyond
Items.Abstract: As reported elsewhere, the Reactive Ion-PLasma Etched (RIPLE) grating technology emerged to show its highly predictive process that resulted in gratings with near theoretical super-broadband diffraction efficiency. The RIPLE process taps into electron-beam (eBeam) patterning and dry reactive-ion etching to embed a nano-scale grating structure into substrate material. Our prior NSF-supported effort succeeded in scaling the process in grating area to 4x4 sq. inch. However, our reliance on the commercially available eBeam services prevents the RIPLE process from scaling in area beyond 5x5 sq. inch. Under new NSF support, we began developing a dedicated large area grating patterning tool called the MAGPIE. It uses a long-travel nano-positioning stage and near-field Talbot effect to inscribe nano-scale grating patterns over very large areas. We discuss the operational principles, system/subsystem designs and prototyping activities so far, and some of the early tests of the MAGPIE.

Items.Authors: Hugues Sana, Bart Vandenbussche, Gert Raskin, Emilie Beevers, Pierre Royer
Items.Title: MUSTI: a Massive star far-Ultraviolet Spectroscopic TIme domain mission
Items.Abstract: With a 40 cm-aperture, MUSTI is a far-ultraviolet (FUV) spectroscopic ESA F-class mission proposal dedicated to time-domain stellar physics. MUSTI combines a tailor-made, high-resolution (R = 20 000), FUV (120-210 nm) échelle spectrograph and a secondary high precision pointing system with a standardised platform. MUSTI will obtain breakthrough  observational constraints on massive stars’ interior physics, stellar winds and binary products.  These novel constraints will enable the precise calibration of the evolution of massive single  and binary stars towards their final fate, with far reaching implications for cosmic models,  the interpretation of the first stars and the first galaxies observed by the James Webb Space  Telescope and inference-based analyses of Gravitational Waves detections.

Items.Authors: Anand Nagesh
Items.Title: Nano-Observatory-as-a-Service (NOaaS): a constellation of suitcase sized CubeSat telescopes for near real-time 3D sky mapping and anomaly detection using AWS-Integrated Professional service to enable virtual observatories
Items.Abstract: Nano Observatory as a Service (NOaaS):A Cloud-Connected Space/Ground Telescope Network for Real-Time Sky Awareness is a new way of monitoring the sky, using a fleet of small telescopes in space, combined with ground observatories and cloud computing on aws, to deliver real-time insights about what is happening above Earth. Instead of relying only on large, expensive observatories, NOaaS uses multiple compact telescopes in low-Earth orbit working together as a virtual global observatory.  In the age of AI and computing we are building a future by transforming how humanity explores space by monetizing access to cosmic events through Leveraging Space/Ground data from network of multispectral ground and In-Orbit Telescopes with accurate AI models for astronomy, education, and Asset/SSA-adjacent space mapping for making it accessible to researchers, students, space asset operators, Insurance company and enthusiasts worldwide using AWS platform.

Items.Authors: Kumiko Morihana, Ichi Tanaka, Shogo Nishiyama
Items.Title: New narrow-band filter system on MOIRCS at the Subaru Telescope
Items.Abstract: Narrow-band imaging can identify emission and absorption features from many sources simultaneously, but continuum subtraction becomes difficult when spectral slopes vary or when equivalent widths are small. We developed a new narrow-band filter set for MOIRCS on the Subaru Telescope that includes a main Br-gamma passband (wavelength center: 2.168 microns, width:0.016 microns) and additional passbands (wavelength center: 2.139, 2.214 microns, width:0.023, 0.018 microns) on both sides of the line. This design enables more accurate continuum estimation than conventional filters that transmit only on one side. On-sky tests confirm that the new system can detect emission lines with small equivalent widths that are often missed by traditional narrow-band imaging. We present the filter design and its demonstrated performance.

Items.Authors: Sylvestre Lacour, Johan Kosmalski, Michael Mueller, Célia Desgrange, Oscar Carrión-González, Mathias Nowak, Elsa Huby, Julien Woillez, Jens Kammerer, Jean-Baptiste Lebouquin, Jason Spyromilio
Items.Title: ngVLTI: Cost and Feasibility of a Four-Telescope VLTI Expansion for Milliarcsecond-Scale Imaging
Items.Abstract: We assess the cost and technical feasibility of extending the Very Large Telescope Interferometer (VLTI) with four additional 8 m Unit Telescopes (UTs), forming the new generation VLTI (ngVLTI). The upgrade would provide dense uv coverage with baselines up to 200 m, enabling milliarcsecond-resolution imaging across a broad range of science cases. We examine a compact telescope concept with a fast (f/0.64), segmented primary mirror feeding a subterranean coudé focus compatible with the existing VLTI. We summarise the optical and mechanical design and present a cost estimate of about €70 million per telescope (2025 prices). Comparison with Keck, Gemini, the VLT UTs, and the ELT suggests the proposed upgrade is both technically feasible and cost-competitive.

Items.Authors: Vincenzo Davide Cardinale, Alfonso Collura, Fabio D’Anca, Andrea Bocchieri, Paolo Chioetto, Riccardo Claudi, Elisa Guerriero, Alberto Gulizzi, Riccardo Lilli, Giuseppe Malaguti, Giuseppina Micela, Emanuele Pace, Enzo Pascale, Paolo Picchi, Giampaolo Preti, Claudio Saitta, Antonio Scippa, Andrea Tozzi, Salvatore Varisco, Paola Zuppella
Items.Title: Non-destructive dynamic characterization of thin Ni-P coatings on Ariel AW6061-T651 mirrors using modal analysis
Items.Abstract: This work presents a non-destructive modal analysis approach for the dynamic characterization of thin Ni-P optical coatings developed for the ESA Ariel mission. Experimental tests on coated aluminum substrates demonstrate that the technique is highly sensitive to coating properties, enabling accurate evaluation of their impact on natural frequencies, mode shapes, and damping. The method provides a complete dynamic fingerprint without altering the sample, supporting coating thickness assessment, FEM model validation, and detection of anisotropic effects. These results contribute to the optimization of high-precision mirror systems, ultimately enhancing Ariel’s capability to deliver accurate spectroscopic data for exoplanet atmosphere studies.

Items.Authors: Alexander Pevtsov, Luca Bertello
Items.Title: NSOs full disk MOF based vector magnetograph concept (MVMC)
Items.Abstract: The Sun's magnetic field serves as the primary driver of solar eruptions. Precise and uninterrupted measurement of the Sun’s magnetic fields are required for predictions of solar eruptive phenomena and evaluating their potential impact on the Earth and on space missions. The primary instrument used by the majority of space weather agencies is NSF's NSO's Global Oscillations Network Group (GONG). GONG employs a modest effective aperture and is only capable of generating line-of-sight (LOS) magnetograms. There are a number of efforts to create networks of Magneto-Optical Filter (MOF) based LOS magnetographs (SAMNet, GATES). However, vector magnetographs have a number of advantages and are the future of the field. The proposed instrument will be capable of continuously producing vector magnetograms. An instrument such this could be used for both groundbased and satellite observatories thus allowing for multi-messenger style missions. We discuss the instrument design and its capabilities.

Items.Authors: Pilar Montañés-Rodríguez, Jose Luis Rasilla Piñeiro, Daniel Fenandez, Ana Fragoso
Items.Title: Numerical analysis of material-removal behaviour in optical polishing processes at the CSOA15 laboratory
Items.Abstract: The Centro de Sistemas Ópticos Avanzados (CSOA) at the Instituto de Astrofísica de Canarias has recently expanded with the creation of CSOA15, a laboratory dedicated to large-aperture optical polishing and coating, with capability for optical surfaces up to 1.5 m in diameter. In CNC optical polishing, the surface change produced by a process can deviate from the programmed correction due to tool behaviour, material properties, machine response, trajectory definition, slurry conditions, and environmental factors. This work analyses interferometric data acquired before and after polishing processes performed at CSOA15. Process-effect maps are extracted from corrected measured surfaces and used to evaluate process variability through mean height change, PV, and RMS. The analysis supports the understanding of measured process behaviour and future process-chain optimisation aimed at reducing manufacturing time while maintaining surface-form quality.

Items.Authors: Derya Öztürk Çetni, Cahit Yeşilyaprak, Jonas Kühn, Laurent Jolissaint
Items.Title: numerical investigation of NCPA-induced coronagraphic performance for the DAG400 telescope
Items.Abstract: This work presents a detailed numerical study of how alignment errors and residual aberrations shape the coronagraphic performance of the 4-meter Eastern Anatolia Observatory (DAG) Telescope. The analysis concentrates on non-common-path (NCP) aberrations, slow mechanical drifts along the optical train, focal-plane mask offsets, Lyot stop misplacements, and shifts introduced during pupil-tracking operation. Together, these effects determine the structure of the final point-spread function and the contrast that can be reached at the near-infrared (NIR) detector.    To examine these contributions in a controlled environment, a Python-based simulation tool - the DAG Coronagraph Numerical Simulator (NoDC) - was developed. Relying on diffraction propagation and a full coronagraphic model, the framework follows how small misalignments evolve through the system and how residual wavefront errors from the active optics (ao) and adaptive optics (AO) stages imprint themselves on the science images.

Items.Authors: Joschua Hellemeier, Paul Hickson, Noelia Martinez Rey
Items.Title: Numerical simulations on the feasibility of polychromatic laser guide stars
Items.Abstract: Polychromatic laser guide stars are one suggested method for tip/tilt retrieval without the use of a natural guide star in adaptive optics systems. For polychromatic laser guide stars, sodium atoms are excited to upper energy levels, use different decay channels to the ground state, and emit light at different wavelengths. Due to dispersion, the light at different wavelengths will show small differences in tip/tilt after propagating through the atmosphere. This differential tip/tilt component can be used to retrieve the total tip/tilt in an adaptive optics system.   We study the feasibility of polychromatic laser guide stars for tip/tilt retrieval by using optical Bloch equations to simulate the excitation of sodium in the mesosphere and by using physical optics to model the propagation of light through the atmosphere.

Items.Authors: Mackenzie F. Carlson, Jack Ford, Stephan R. McCandliss, Emily Witt, Alexander S. Kutyrev, Suryakanthi Srinivas Rachamadugu, Kyowon Kim, Meng-Ping Chang, Paul A. Scowen, Edward J. Wollack
Items.Title: OAxFORTIS: FUV investigations of hot stars in globular clusters
Items.Abstract: The Off-Axis Far-UV Off Rowland-circle Telescope for Imaging and Spectroscopy (OAxFORTIS) is an off-axis reconfiguration of the sounding rocket experiment, FORTIS, designed to conduct multi-object spectroscopy. OAxFORTIS enables the investigation of the UV diversity of the hot horizontal branch (HHB) in the otherwise similar globular clusters M10, M13, and M3. This exploration is intended to address a question commonly referred to as the "Second Parameter Problem" as researchers hunt for parameters other than metallicity that drive this diversity. The first flight of OAxFORTIS took place on August 2024 and resulted in the successful observation of M10, with at least 3 strong stellar spectra acquired. Preparations for the second launch include the installation of XeLIF optical coatings and a new Next Generation microshutter array.

Items.Authors: Evgeniy A. Kopylov, Michael Sachkov, Sergey Sichevsky, Yuriy Kazakevich
Items.Title: On the ground support facilities of the Spektr-UF mission
Items.Abstract: Observational data in the ultraviolet region of the electromagnetic spectrum (115-305 nm) are a powerful tool for studying many astrophysical objects, such as exoplanets, especially for determining the characteristics of their atmospheres. Work is underway to create the Spektr-UV orbital space Observatory (World Space Observatory - Ultraviolet), which will succeed the Hubble Space Telescope. The Institute of Astronomy of the Russian Academy of Sciences is the leading scientific organization of this project. Within the framework of this study, work is planned to determine the characteristics for creating instruments for ground support of missions, to develop tools for preparing applications for an observation program, and to develop a scientific research program for the project.

Items.Authors: Simone Chiarucci, Giovanni Giusi, Andrea Russi, Mauro Focardi, Anna Maria Di Giorgio, Rosario Cosentino, Marina Vela Nunez, Scigè John Liù, Maria Farina, Fulvio De Persio
Items.Title: On-board control procedures for autonomous alignment of science production and hardware compression for the PLATO Mission
Items.Abstract: The PLATO mission requires twenty-four Normal Cameras (NCAMs) to operate coherently for high-precision photometry. To prevent data stream corruption, the Instrument Control Unit (ICU) must align data production to a strict 6.25s acquisition slot. This paper presents a specialized On-Board Control Procedure (OBCP) designed to manage this synchronization. We describe the nominal start-up sequence, utilizing a reference NCAM event to trigger simultaneous observation and hardware compression, ensuring phase coherence. Furthermore, we detail the autonomous FDIR logic executed following an ICU reboot at the L2 Lagrange point. This sequence restores the Payload Configuration Vector (PCV) and re-initializes N-DPUs to re-establish valid data chunking without ground support. Implemented via interpreted OCL scripts, this architecture allows for dynamic decision-making and in-flight updates.

Items.Authors: John T. Rayner, Mike Connelley, Adwin Boogert, Kenji Emerson, Mike Kelii, Dan Kokubun, Charles Lockhart, Jim Thorne
Items.Title: One-shot 0.4-4.2-micron integral field R=250 spectrograph and imager for the NASA IRTF
Items.Abstract: SPECTRE is a new low-resolution (R≈250) integral-field spectrograph and imager that provides continuous 0.4–4.2 μm wavelength coverage in a single exposure. Built at the University of Hawai’i for first light on the 3.2-m IRTF in 2028, its science drivers include rapid characterization of NEOs, small solar system bodies, and optical-infrared transients.  The instrument uses two dichroics to split the beam into optical, near-IR, and mid-IR channels feeding a 2k×2k frame-transfer CCD and two H2RG arrays, all operated by Archon controllers. A 7.2″×7.2″ image-slicer IFU provides slit-loss-free spectroscopy, and each channel employs a mirror-based collimator-camera with dual-pass prisms. For stability the bench-mounted optics and arrays contain no moving parts. The optics and arrays are cryogenically cooled by one closed-cycle cooler.   Acquisition and guiding use a 3′×3′ warm CCD camera, with optional on-object near-IR guiding from rapid H2RG reads. We summarize the design and status.

Items.Authors: Qihang Zhang, Shuangquan Chen, Yonggang Gu, Zhen Zhang
Items.Title: Online upgradeable fiber positioning drive system for LAMOST
Items.Abstract: The LAMOST Phase II project has entered a critical stage, and a miniaturized driver board has been designed for the new integrated fiber positioner. In terms of hardware, a 6-layer PCB with a compact layout is adopted, with an overall board size of 142×14 mm, covering power supply, main control, driver, and communication modules, which can realize parallel control of six BLDC motors and triple the control efficiency. In terms of software, a precise open-loop drive algorithm is used to control the BLDC motors,a self-inspectable motor control logic is designed, data and commands are received under a CAN communication network, and remote online hardware program upgrade can be realized via IAP, which improves the efficiency of system maintenance and upgrade. Finally, an experimental platform is built for verification. Multiple fiber positioning tests demonstrate that 98.86% of positioning errors are less than 20μm, which satisfies the high-precision positioning requirements of the LAMOST.

Items.Authors: Jin-Ah Kim, Haeun Chung, Miriam Keppler, Aafaque Khan, Carlos Vargas, Erika Hamden
Items.Title: On-orbit calibration plan for the Aspera FUV SmallSat
Items.Abstract: Aspera is a SmallSat mission funded by the NASA Astrophysics Pioneers program. Aspera will be launched in 2027 and is designed to observe diffuse O VI emission at 103.2nm from the circumgalactic medium of nearby galaxies. The payload consists of two long-slit spectrographs with a field of view of 1 degree by 36 arcsec. We have developed calibration methods to measure astrometric solutions, dispersion relationships, and effective area curves using on-orbit observations. In our presentation, we will describe our observational plans and analysis strategies for the calibration.

Items.Authors: Zhengjiang Zhang, Huatao Zhang, Yanbing Chen, Tong Zhou, Kai Zhang, Mingda Jiang, Zhen Tang
Items.Title: On-site integration and commissioning of a high-resolution echelle spectrograph for the 1.2m astronomical telescope of Sun Yat-Sen University
Items.Abstract: The astronomical high dispersion spectrograph for the 1.2-meter astronomical telescope is a fiber-fed, high-resolution echelle spectrograph located at the astronomical station of Zhuhai campus of Sun Yat-Sen University. It is fed by the Cassegrain focus via a 25-meter-long, 2.7’’ optical fiber. The spectrograph provides spectral resolution higher than 30000 over the wavelength range of 400-900nm. It enables the science team to do frontier researches and education in astronomical fields such as chemical element abundance measurement, stellar formation and evolution. This paper mainly describes the spectrograph alignment and the commissioning performance. We adopted a method of combining autocollimation with Knife-Edge test to intuitively and precisely align the optical axis of each optical component, and improve working efficiency. With the commissioning observations, the instrumental performance has been further optimized and met the scientific requirements.

Items.Authors: Mirko Colapietro, Sergio D'Orsi, Salvatore Savarese, Pietro Schipani, Laurent Marty, Giulio Capasso, Ricardo Zanmar Sánchez, Kalyan Radhakrishnan Santhakumari, Federico Battaini, Simone Di Filippo, Matteo Aliverti, Simone Doniselli, Andrea Baruffolo, Davide Ricci, Bernardo Salasnich, Paolo D'Avanzo, Sergio Campana, Riccardo Claudi, David Young, Marco Landoni, Matteo Munari, Stephen Smartt, Matteo Genoni, Fabrizio Vitali, Salvatore Scuderi, Rosario Cosentino, Frédéric Dérie, Markus Schoeller, Armin Silber, Ivo Saviane, Emanuela Pompei, Derek Ives, Antonio Miccichè, Gaetano Nicotra, Eugenio Martinetti, Silvio Di Rosa, Marco Dima, Adam Rubin, Marco Riva, Michael Rappaport, Giuliano Pignata, Luigi Lessio, Hanindyo Kuncarayakti, Ofir Hershko, Francesco D'Alessio, Anna Brucalassi, Alex Bichkovsky, Sagi Ben-Ami, José Antonio Araiza-Durán, Maximilian Stritzinger, Seppo Mattila, Avishay Gal-Yam, Iair Arcavi, Massimo Della Valle, Enrico Cappellaro, Antonio Sulich, Jani Achrén, Marcos Hernandez Diaz, Jari Kotilainen, Gianluca Li Causi, Hector Pérez Ventura
Items.Title: On-site integration and validation of the SOXS control electronics at ESO-NTT
Items.Abstract: The Son Of X-Shooter (SOXS) instrument is a dual-arm, wide-band spectrograph designed to provide rapid and flexible follow-up observations of transient phenomena with the ESO NTT.  After successfully completing its Preliminary Acceptance in Europe at the end of 2024, the instrument was shipped to the ESO La Silla Observatory.  This paper presents the on-site integration and validation of the SOXS control electronics.  We describe the tests performed at the telescope, including hardware integration, verification of network and software interfaces, functional checks of the motion and thermal control systems, and communication tests with the instrument control software.  Particular emphasis is placed on the assessment of timing stability, electromagnetic compatibility within the telescope environment, and system robustness under operational constraints such as temperature variations and safety interlocks, highlighting lessons learned that guided the optimization of the system.

Items.Authors: Rasjied Sloot, Rudy Wijnands, Steven Bloemen, Hans Ellermeijer, Alexander Hoogerbrug, Rik ter Horst
Items.Title: On-sky commissioning and technical performance of Proto-NUX at Pic du Midi
Items.Abstract: The Near-Ultraviolet eXplorer (NUX) is a proposed ground-based observing facility designed to expand near-ultraviolet (NUV) astronomy by enabling observations in the 300--350 nm range from Earth. To validate this concept, a single-telescope prototype, Proto-NUX, was commissioned at the Pic du Midi Observatory in the French Pyrenees during its first high-altitude observing campaign in March 2026. The campaign tested deployment, remote operation, calibration, detector performance, image quality, tracking, and simultaneous optical monitoring under realistic observing conditions. In particular, the delivered NUV point-spread function was broader than expected, likely due to residual collimation, chromatic effects, and internal reflections. The detector dark current contributed significantly to the noise budget. We discuss limitations and key improvements for future Proto-NUX campaigns and the NUX system.

Items.Authors: Aditi Desai, Stephanie E. Sallum, Andrew J. Skemer
Items.Title: On-sky demonstration of speckle noise removal using the SCALES medium-spectral-resolution mode
Items.Abstract: The Slicer Combined with Array of Lenslets for Exoplanet Spectroscopy (SCALES) is a 2-5 micron high-contrast lenslet-based integral field spectrograph (IFS) designed to detect and characterize exoplanets. The SCALES medium-resolution mode comprises a lenslet subarray with a 0.34 x 0.36 arcsecond field of view (FOV) and an image slicer, allowing for measurements of molecular abundances and disequilibrium chemistry in giant exoplanet atmospheres at increased spectral resolution. This mode uses a piezo-electric mirror to offset the FOV from the star to the planet. We use SCALES commissioning data to perform tests on speckle noise removal software designed specifically for observations this mode, employing angular and spectral differential imaging to mitigate stellar, atmospheric, and instrumental noise effects. We demonstrate the achievable contrast for the medium-resolution mode and use the results to estimate our ability to recover planet signals and characterize exoplanet atmospheres.

Items.Authors: Roland Winkler, Weijia Sun, Daniel Sablowski, Thomas Liebner, Ole Streicher, Steffen Frey, Ingo Stilz, Alexander Pramskiy, Scott Smedley, Thomas Szeifert, Diogo Rio Fernandes, Gerard Zins
Items.Title: On-sky fibre-target-alignment of the 4MOST instrument: calibration and performance
Items.Abstract: The 4-metre Multi-Object Spectroscopic Telescope (4MOST) is a new wide-field, fibre-fed spectroscopic survey facility for the VISTA telescope at ESO’s Paranal Observatory. The instrument enables the simultaneous acquisition of 2436 spectra across a 4.2 deg² field of view, using a tilting spine fibre positioner feeding three dedicated spectrographs. In this paper, we describe the final calibration process, and performance verification of the Fibre-Target-Alignment (FTA) for 4MOST on the VISTA telescope. We show how reach a final positioning performance of approximately 16u m / 0.27 arc sec relative to targets on sky.
